name: Adam Henriksson
body: Assuming the classical Riemann hypothesis, we answer Erd\H{o}s problem~462 affirmatively even when the sum is restricted to composite integers. For every real $x\ge 9.6\cdot10^{37}$, the open interval $(x,x+384\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2)$ contains at least $(14/3)\sqrt{x}$ distinct products of two primes of size comparable to $\sqrt{x}$. Their contribution to the sum of the least prime factor divided by the integer is at least $14/9$. For every fixed interval coefficient $C>0$, the composite sum is bounded above unconditionally and bounded away from zero under the Riemann hypothesis, for all sufficiently large $x$. We present a computer-assisted proof, verified in Lean~4. The formalization takes the cited estimates for primes as inputs. The results have not been independently reviewed.
